recommendation: Keep the no-change audit as-is. Add new ServiceRequest boundary prose only if a current Patient Care or Orders and Observations decision requests it; FHIR-5510 itself is sufficiently represented by historical application, related FHIR-6196 handling, and later resource consolidation.
issue_request: FHIR-5510 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Care DSTU1 clarification asking to improve Boundaries text differentiating ProcedureRequest, DiagnosticOrder/DiagnosticRequest, and ReferralRequest, because implementers saw multiple ways to model the same requested service such as an imaging test.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly names FHIR-5510. Early Patient Care introduction updates appear to have applied it implicitly: f57e1dc9b9cab13e93ba2615f610ea05bfc962cc added ReferralRequest boundary guidance against DiagnosticOrder and ProcedureRequest, and 07aa93633f66b8d2d0b94692528feae41659d399 added matching ProcedureRequest boundary guidance, including overlap and search-across-resources advice.
additional_context: FHIR-6196 is the concrete later Published/Persuasive issue in the same boundary family and is already represented on the combined branch by commit 8393152c9d4f075fab4cf4410b82576a683af2f8. Later source history consolidated the relevant resources: DiagnosticOrder became DiagnosticRequest, DiagnosticRequest was merged into ProcedureRequest, ProcedureRequest was renamed to ServiceRequest, and ReferralRequest was merged into that same lineage. source/fhir.ini now marks ServiceRequest as active while DiagnosticOrder, ProcedureRequest, and ReferralRequest are recorded as subsumed/merged/renamed into ServiceRequest. Current ServiceRequest source covers diagnostic tests, procedures, specialist consultation/referral-style use, request workflow, resulting resources, and boundaries with Task and CommunicationRequest. Zulip and Confluence searches found no directly relevant conflicting evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Reintroducing the obsolete DSTU1 comparison among ProcedureRequest, DiagnosticOrder/DiagnosticRequest, and ReferralRequest into current ServiceRequest would revive retired resource distinctions and duplicate current merged-resource guidance without changing implementer understanding.
